binders: Universally quantify an implicit natural number m, with m = 0 permitted.
Universally quantify a matrix A : Fin m → Fin m → Real.
On the left side, existentially quantify λ : Fin m → Real and then a basis b indexed by Fin m of the real vector space Fin m → Real; require an equation for every p : Fin m.
On the right side, existentially quantify μ : Fin m → Real and then v : Fin m → (Fin m → Real); require an equation for every p : Fin m.

The witnesses on each side may depend on m and A. Within each side the vector or basis witness is quantified after the eigenvalue family. The existential witnesses on opposite sides are separately bound.
hypotheses: There are no additional assumptions on m or A beyond m being a natural number and A being a real m by m matrix.
conclusions: There exists a real basis b of Real^m and a real scalar λ_p for each basis vector, satisfying A b_p = λ_p b_p for every p, if and only if there exist m linearly independent vectors v_p in Real^m and real scalars μ_p satisfying A v_p = μ_p v_p for every p.
Both implications are asserted. Neither side is asserted to hold for every matrix independently of the equivalence.
mathematical_definitions: Fin m consists of the indices 0, 1, ..., m − 1; Real^m is represented as the function space Fin m → Real.
For a vector w, the i-th coordinate of A w is the finite sum over j : Fin m of A(i,j)w(j).
Scalar multiplication is coordinatewise: (c w)(i) = c w(i). Thus each eigenvector equation asserts the corresponding equality at every coordinate.
Linear independence over Real means that if the sum over p : Fin m of c_p v_p equals the zero vector, then every real coefficient c_p is zero.
A basis gives each vector of Real^m a unique representation as a finite real linear combination of its indexed vectors.
The left-hand predicate is precisely existence of a basis consisting of real eigenvectors, equivalently diagonalizability over Real.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative integer m and every real m by m matrix A, A admits a basis of Real^m consisting of eigenvectors with real eigenvalues if and only if there are m linearly independent vectors in Real^m, each satisfying an eigenvector equation for some real eigenvalue. All eigenvalues and vectors are chosen as indexed families. On the right, linear independence and the eigenvector equations must hold simultaneously for those same vectors.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is restricted to finite square matrices over Real, with eigenvectors and linear independence also over Real.

There is no positive-dimension hypothesis. When m = 0, the eigenvector equations have no instances, the empty vector family is linearly independent, and the zero-dimensional space has an empty basis; both sides hold.

For an inhabited index type, linear independence implies that each chosen vector is nonzero. A separate nonzero-vector conjunct is therefore unnecessary; the eigenvector equations alone would not ensure this.
Eigenvalues need not be distinct, nonzero, positive, ordered, or uniquely listed. Repeated eigenvalues are allowed.
The basis and independent vectors are not required to be orthogonal, normalized, or quantitatively well-conditioned.

Spanning is explicit through the basis witness on the left. On the right it follows mathematically from having m independent vectors in the m-dimensional space, rather than appearing as a separate conjunct.
There is no symmetry, invertibility, or other structural assumption on A.
The proposition does not assert that every real square matrix admits these witnesses, nor does it equate merely having real eigenvalues with admitting an eigenbasis.
No parameter-dependent regularity, differential equation, stability estimate, or norm bound is encoded.
